q: So is this a website problem or an ads problem?
answer:
This looks like more of a customer/acquisition problem than a website breakdown: orders fell 12.4% (210 → 184) but the statistical diagnosis identifies the drop in customers as a supported cause — customers fell 22.0% (214 → 167) and the engine estimates that explains most of the orders loss. Ad spend rose slightly, so spend itself did not cause the decline.

- What moved: Customers 214 → 167 (−22.0%) — identified as a cause; Sessions 20,645 → 16,632 (−19.4%) moved with orders but the analysis flags it as correlation (may be reacting rather than causing). 
- Ads and clicks: Ad spend ₹2,98,777 → ₹3,00,853 (+0.7%) moved opposite to orders and is ruled out as a cause. Clicks fell (27,954 → 18,449, −34.0%) and are outside their usual range, but the causal test shows raw association disappears after controlling for calendar and competing drivers — not a supported cause.
- Website behaviour blind spots: PDP-level metrics (page views, add-to-cart, purchase rate) were not available for this scope and could not be tested; that means a conversion funnel problem on PDPs cannot be ruled out from the data we have.

Worth checking: 1) Break down the customer and sessions drop by acquisition channel (paid vs organic) and campaign to see whether acquisition fell; 2) Pull PDP page-views → add-to-cart → purchase rate by channel to confirm whether conversion on-site changed.

Period: 2026-10-19 to 2026-10-25 · Currency: INR · Data as of 2026-10-29
